title: Essentials first (Avot 3:18)
hookLine: Elazar Chisma: the core laws are the essentials; clever calculations are the dessert
tomorrow: what does a good deed pay? the answer is strange.

cards: Every group project has someone who builds gorgeous slides and someone who actually read the assignment. The Talmud tells of a ship at sea.

Rabban Gamliel finds that Rabbi Yehoshua packed extra flour, because Yehoshua had worked out from the stars that the voyage might run long. Gamliel says: you know all this, and you still travel by ship?

Yehoshua answers: don't wonder at me. Wonder at two of your students on land, Elazar Chisma and Yochanan ben Gudgada. They can reckon the drops in the sea, and they have no bread to eat and no clothes to wear.

teach.b: Rabban Gamliel noticed. The story says he sent for the two of them and gave them positions, so they'd have a living.
And here's the turn: that same Elazar Chisma, the one who could reckon the sea, is the voice of today's line in Avot. Kinin u-fitchei niddah, hen hen gufei halachot.
The laws of bird offerings and the laws of a couple's private life: these are the body of the law.
Tekufot ve-gematriaot, parparaot lachochmah: the reckoning of seasons and number-play are the side dishes of wisdom.
Kinin were the pair of birds the Torah lets a new mother bring when she can't afford a lamb.
So the essentials, for him, are where the law touches an ordinary household, and the poor. The calculations he was well-known for, he calls dessert. Not useless: dessert is good.
Just not dinner. The man who could count the sea put a poor mother's two birds first.

how: Avot 3:18 is studied with the Talmud's shipboard story in Horayot 10a; teachers use it to ask which parts of practice touch real people first.

o: the plain core of the law before clever extras
the foods eaten before a festival's sweets
a list of the oldest laws in the Torah

games.q: the body and the dessert — tap the pairs.

s: Elazar Chisma thought astronomy and number-play were useless
he calls them side dishes of wisdom: good, just not dinner.
in the Talmud's story, Elazar Chisma could reckon the drops of the sea and had no bread
Rabbi Yehoshua says so, and Rabban Gamliel steps in.
the essentials Elazar names are the Temple's grand ceremonies
kinin are a poor family's offering; the essentials touch ordinary homes.

games.q: you're planning your cousin's bar mitzvah party: a slick video montage, or making sure grandma's ride and the kosher meals are set. Elazar Chisma would say:
o: the ride and the meals first; the montage is dessert.
the montage, since that's what people will remember.
skip both; the ceremony is the only thing that matters.
games.why: his body of the law is where it touches real households; the clever extras come after.

practice: On a scrap of paper, write the few things on your plate this week. Circle the one where a real person is counting on you: that's the body of the law.
Put a small star beside the clever extra you'd rather be doing, and let it wait as dessert.

wordCard.voice: Essentials first. Elazar Chisma's gufei halachot, the body of the law, before the clever dessert.

orig.note: Hebrew: the bodies of the law, Elazar Chisma's phrase for the essentials.

carryVoice: Essentials first, and the dessert after, with no guilt at all. Good night, or good morning.

sources.ref: Babylonian Talmud, Horayot 10a (Gamliel and Yehoshua at sea)
Leviticus 12:8 (a mother who can't afford a lamb brings two birds)
